sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Type / MCQs / Assertion-Reasoning

questions.question_text: Which vitamin prevents the deficiency disease known as scurvy, maintaining healthy gums?
questions.answer: C) Vitamin C

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): A freely suspended bar magnet always points in the North-South direction.
Reason (R): The Earth behaves like a huge magnet with its magnetic poles near its geographical poles.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: What is the standard International System (SI) unit for measuring length?
questions.answer: C) Meter

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of periodic motion?
options: A) A car moving on a straight road
B) The swinging pendulum of a clock
C) A mango falling from a tree
D) A butterfly flying in a garden
questions.answer: B) The swinging pendulum of a clock

questions.question_text: Which of these materials allows light to pass through it completely?
questions.answer: C) Clear glass

questions.question_text: Animals that eat only plants or plant products are classified as:
questions.answer: B) Herbivores

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Cooking pans are usually made of metals like aluminum or copper.
Reason (R): Metals are good conductors of heat and allow food to cook faster.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: How many meters make up one kilometer?
questions.answer: C) 1000 meters

questions.question_text: What happens when the South pole of one magnet is brought near the South pole of another magnet?
questions.answer: B) They repel each other

questions.question_text: Which chemical solution is used to test the presence of starch in a food item?
questions.answer: C) Iodine solution

questions.question_text: Which of the following materials is soluble in water?
questions.answer: C) Sugar

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Green plants are called autotrophs.
Reason (R): Green plants can prepare their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a magnetic material?
questions.answer: C) Iron

questions.question_text: The motion of a drawer being opened and closed is an example of:
questions.answer: B) Rectilinear motion

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Dietary fibers or roughage do not provide any nutrients to our body.
Reason (R): Roughage is essential as it helps our body get rid of undigested food.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: What part of a bar magnet has the strongest magnetic pull?
options: B) At its North and South poles
C) Only at the North pole
D) The magnetic pull is uniform everywhere
questions.answer: B) At its North and South poles

questions.question_text: A metal spoon appears shiny. This property of materials is known as:
questions.answer: D) Lustre

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Handspan cannot be used as a standard unit of length.
Reason (R): The length of a handspan varies from person to person.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: A disease caused by the deficiency of Iodine in the diet is:
questions.answer: A) Goiter

questions.question_text: If a bar magnet is broken into two halves, what is the result?
options: A) One half becomes only a North pole, the other a South pole
B) They lose their magnetism completely
C) Each half becomes a complete magnet with a North and South pole
D) They turn into non-magnetic materials
questions.answer: C) Each half becomes a complete magnet with a North and South pole

questions.question_text: Why do we need standard units of measurement instead of using body parts like handspans? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Body parts like handspans vary in size from person to person, leading to inaccurate and inconsistent measurements. Standard units ensure uniformity and exactness globally.

questions.question_text: How should bar magnets be safely stored to prevent them from losing their magnetism? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Bar magnets should be stored in pairs with opposite poles on the same side, separated by wood, and with soft iron keepers across their ends.

questions.question_text: What is meant by a 'balanced diet'? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A balanced diet is one that contains all essential nutrients—carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals—in the correct proportions, along with adequate water and roughage.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between transparent and opaque objects using one example for each. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Transparent objects, like clear glass, allow light to pass through completely. Opaque objects, like a wooden board, completely block light from passing through.

questions.question_text: Provide two examples of periodic motion from your daily life. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Two examples of periodic motion are the swinging of a playground swing and the rhythmic beating of a human heart.

questions.question_text: Why do aquatic plants generally have poorly developed root systems? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Aquatic plants are surrounded by water, so their roots do not need to seek moisture deep underground; their main function is just to anchor the plant.

questions.question_text: Explain the importance of proteins in our diet. Name one plant source and one animal source of protein. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Proteins are body-building foods essential for the growth, repair, and maintenance of our body tissues. A common plant source of protein is soybean or lentils, and an animal source is milk or eggs.

questions.question_text: How can you find geographic directions using a simple bar magnet if you do not have a compass? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Tie a thread to the center of the bar magnet and suspend it freely. When it comes to rest, it will align itself in the North-South direction. The end pointing North indicates geographic North.

questions.question_text: Why are cooking utensils generally made of metals, but their handles are made of wood or hard plastic? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Cooking utensils are made of metals because they are good conductors of heat, helping cook food efficiently. Handles are made of wood or plastic because they are insulators, protecting our hands from getting burned.

questions.question_text: Describe the correct method to measure the length of a curved line using a simple thread. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Place a thread precisely along the curved line, marking the starting and ending points on the thread. Then, straighten the thread and measure the distance between the two marks using a standard meter scale.

questions.question_text: Classify animals into three categories based on their food habits and provide one example for each. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Animals are classified as herbivores (plant-eaters like cows), carnivores (meat-eaters like lions), and omnivores (eating both plants and animals like humans or crows).

questions.question_text: Differentiate between rectilinear motion and circular motion, providing a suitable example for each type. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Rectilinear motion occurs when an object moves in a straight line, like a car on a straight highway. Circular motion is when an object moves along a circular path, like the blades of a ceiling fan.

questions.question_text: What are deficiency diseases? Name the disease caused by a severe lack of Iron and state its main symptom. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Deficiency diseases are illnesses caused by a prolonged lack of specific nutrients in the diet. A lack of iron causes anemia, which is characterized by extreme weakness, fatigue, and pale skin.

questions.question_text: What happens when the North pole of one magnet is brought near the North pole of a second magnet, and then near the South pole? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: When the North pole approaches another North pole, they repel each other due to the rule that like poles repel. When brought near a South pole, they attract each other because opposite poles attract.

questions.question_text: A student rides a bicycle from home to school on a straight road. Identify and explain the two different types of motion exhibited by the bicycle wheels. Furthermore, explain how you would measure the exact distance from home to school accurately using a measuring tape. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The bicycle wheels exhibit circular motion as they rotate on their axles, and rectilinear motion as they move forward along the straight road. To measure the exact distance, lay a standard measuring tape straight along the path end-to-end, counting the segments, avoiding bends, and reading the standard meter markings carefully.

questions.question_text: Read the case: Rohan eats a daily diet consisting only of white rice, fried potatoes, and sugary sweets. Analyze his diet. Identify which major nutrient groups are missing, predict the potential health issues he might face, and suggest three specific food additions to make his diet balanced. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Rohan's diet is rich in carbohydrates and fats but lacks proteins, vitamins, and minerals. He may suffer from stunted growth, weak immunity, and deficiency diseases like scurvy or anemia. To balance his diet, he must add pulses or eggs for protein, green vegetables for minerals, and fresh fruits for vitamins.

questions.question_text: Describe an experimental activity to test whether different materials (salt, sand, sugar, and sawdust) are soluble or insoluble in water. Clearly state the steps you would take and the expected observations for each of the four materials. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Take four glass tumblers filled with water. Add salt to the first, sand to the second, sugar to the third, and sawdust to the fourth. Stir vigorously and wait. Observation: Salt and sugar will disappear entirely, proving they are soluble. Sand will settle at the bottom, and sawdust will float, proving they are insoluble.

questions.question_text: Explain a step-by-step method to magnetize an ordinary iron nail using a permanent bar magnet (the single-touch method). How can you scientifically test if the iron nail has successfully become a magnet? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Place the iron nail on a table. Stroke it with one pole of a bar magnet from one end to the other, lifting and repeating the motion in the same direction 30-40 times. To test if it is magnetized, bring small iron pins near it; if the nail attracts them, it has successfully become a magnet.
